title: 3D Cell-Printed Hypoxic Cancer-on-a-Chip for Recapitulating Pathologic Progression of Solid Cancer
protocol: Run a 3D CAD software.
Sketch the geometry model of hypoxic cancer-on-a-chip.
Click on Sketch and select the desired plane to draw the geometry.
Set the thickness of the geometry by clicking on Feature-Protrusion Boss/Base.
Enter the desired thickness in the empty box and select the green check icon to form the 3D geometry.
Save the geometry file as a 3D CAD file format (.prt or .stl).
Run a physical diffusion simulation program.
Click on LiveLink and select the CAD program used.
Click on Synchronize to import the geometry of the hypoxic cancer-on-a-chip on the simulation program.
Define the imported 3D geometry as a control volume for oxygen diffusion.
Run computer analysis for gas diffusion using established methods.
Export estimated oxygen concentration data over cross-section A-A' at each time point.
Evaluate whether minimal oxygen level reaches hypoxia threshold.
Repeat computer analysis process with adjusted cellular density if necessary.
Confirm number of cells required to generate oxygen gradient inducing hypoxia.

Place 12 mL of high-glucose Dulbecco's modified Eagle medium containing 10% fetal bovine serum, 100 U/mL penicillin, and 100 μg/mL streptomycin in a T-75 cell culture flask in a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator for 30 min.
Place 12 mL of endothelial cell growth medium in a T-75 cell culture flask in a 5% CO2 humidified incubator at 37°C for 30 min.
Move cryovials containing 5 x 10^5 U-87 MG cells and HUVECs from the liquid nitrogen container to a laminar flow cabinet.
Loosen and retighten the cap of each cryovial immediately after removal to release internal pressure.
Gently place cryopreserved cells in a water bath at 37 °C for 2 min with cap out of water.
Rinse vials with 70% ethanol under laminar flow to prevent contamination.
Transfer thawed cells to flasks containing prepared cell culture media.
Place cell-containing flasks in a 5% CO2 humidified incubator at 37 °C for cell recovery.
Refresh the cell culture media every 2 days and maintain cell growth.
After 24 h of thawing, replace the cell culture media to avoid cytotoxicity of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Use HUVECs that have undergone less than 6 passages.
Prepare a solution of 0.1 N hydrochloric acid (HCl) and filter it with a 0.2 µm syringe filter.
Cut collagen sponges into 5 x 5 mm² pieces and weigh them to total 30 mg for the pre-gel solution.
Transfer cut collagen pieces to a sterile 10 mL glass vial.
Add 2.4 mL of 0.1 N HCl to the collagen-containing glass vial.
Incubate on rocker at 15 rpm and 4 °C for 3 days.
Sieve undigested collagen particles using a 40 µm cell strainer.
Store acidic collagen solution at 4 °C and use within 7 days.
Centrifuge acidic collagen solution at 1224 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Add 30 µL of phenol red solution to the collagen pre-gel solution as a pH indicator.
Add 300 µL of 10x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) buffer to the collagen pre-gel solution.
Neutralize the pH to 7 by adding 240 µL of 1 N sodium hydroxide (NaOH).
Adjust total volume to 3 mL with distilled water.
Store neutralized collagen pre-gel solution at 4 °C and use within 3 days.
Make 50 µL collagen droplets on a small dish using a positive displacement pipette.
Incubate collagen droplets in a 37 °C incubator for 1 h to check gelation.
Check whether the color of collagen has changed into opaque white from transparent.
Tilt container and verify if collagen is adhered to the bottom.
Pour 1x PBS on the droplets and confirm collagen construct does not break in solution.
Generate the 3D geometry of the sacrificial PEVA mold using a 3D CAD software.
Convert the 3D CAD file into an STL file format by clicking on File | Save-File type as STL and Option | Output form as ASCII.
Click on File | Open STL file to import the generated STL file.
Slice the model of the STL-CAD exchanger to automatically generate the G-code for the sacrificial PEVA mold.
Prepare a sterile adhesive and hydrophilic histology slide.
Print the sacrificial PEVA mold on the slide with a 50 G precision nozzle at a pneumatic pressure of 500 kPa at 110 °C.
Mix 6 mL PDMS base elastomer with 0.6 mL curing agent homogenously over 5 min in a plastic reservoir.
Load the blended PDMS solution into a 10 mL disposable syringe.
Fit the syringe head with a 20 G plastic tapered dispense tip.
Fill the sacrificial PEVA mold with the blended PDMS solution from the syringe.
Cure the PDMS barrier in an oven at 40 °C for over 36 hours to avoid melting the PEVA.
Detach the sacrificial PEVA mold with precision tweezers.
Sterilize the gas-permeable barrier at 120 °C in an autoclave.
Wash cancer and stromal cells with 10 mL of 1x PBS using a serological pipette.
Treat the cells with 2 mL of 0.25% trypsin-EDTA using a pipette.
Incubate the treated cells for 3 min at 37 °C.
Neutralize the trypsinized cells with 3 mL of cell culture media.
Collect the suspensions into 15 mL conical tubes and centrifuge at 516 x g for 5 min at 20 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant slowly.
Resuspend the cell pellets in 5 mL cell culture media.
Count the number of cells using a hemocytometer.
Transfer 5 x 10^6 cells of each type into new 15 mL conical tubes.
Centrifuge the cells at 516 x g for 5 min at 20 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant off and place it on wet ice.
Mix cancer cells with the 1% neutralized collagen pre-gel solution on wet ice.
Mix stromal cells with the 1% neutralized collagen pre-gel solution on wet ice.
Resuspend each type of cell pellet with 20 µL of cell culture media.
Add 1 mL of 1% neutralized collagen pre-gel solution to each resuspended cell suspension.
Mix the cell suspensions homogenously using a positive displacement pipette.
Transfer the cell-encapsulated collagen bioinks into 3 mL disposable syringes using a positive displacement pipette.
Store the syringes at 4 °C until 3D cell-printing.
Generate the 3D geometry of cancer-stroma concentric rings using a 3D CAD software.
Convert the 3D CAD file into an STL file format.
Generate a G-code for the cancer-stroma concentric rings using an STL-CAD exchanger.
Load the cell-encapsulated collagen bioinks from 3 mL disposable syringes to the head of the 3D printer.
Set the temperature of the head and plate of the printer to 15 °C.
Load the printing path on the 3D printer control software.
Click the Start button to print collagen bioinks encapsulating cells on the gas-permeable barrier.
Print with an 18 G plastic needle at pneumatic pressure of approximately 20 kPa and maintain a temperature of 15 °C.
Place a sterilized 22 mm x 50 mm glass cover manually on top of the gas-permeable barrier after printing.
Compare groups based on presence or absence of the glass cover to verify hypoxic gradient generation.
Generate three hypoxic cancer-on-chips and transfer them to an incubator at 37 °C for 1 h to cross-link collagen bioinks.
Gently rub cover glasses on top of gas-permeable barriers with a cell-scrapper for tight bonding after fabrication.
Introduce 1.5 mL of endothelial cell growth medium to each chip using pipette, tilting the chip to allow media flow from one side.
Refresh the cell culture media every day for a week.
Use a pipette to aspirate the cell culture medium.
Warm 1x PBS in a water bath at 37 °C.
Prepare the assay solution by adding 0.75 µL of calcein AM and 3 µL of EthD-1 to 1.5 mL pre-warmed PBS.
Aspirate all media from the chip using a pipette.
Wash the cancer construct with prewarmed PBS.
Fill 1.5 mL PBS into the chip using a pipette.
Let the chip stand for 10 min at room temperature.
Introduce 1x PBS from one side of the chips and tilt to allow PBS to flow.
Aspirate the PBS from the chip.
Treat the 1.5 mL assay solution and incubate the chip at 37 °C for 20 min using a foil to protect from light.
Use a pipette to aspirate 1x PBS.
View and capture the labeled cells using a fluorescence microscope.
Count the number of live and dead cells using imaging software.
Prepare 1x PBS at room temperature.
Aspirate all media from the chip using a pipette.
Rinse the chip three times with 1x PBS.
Introduce 1x PBS to the chip from one side and tilt it for even flow.
Let the chip stand with 1x PBS for 5 min between washing steps.
Add 500 μL of 4% PFA to the cancer construct using a pipette.
Leave the PFA solution on the cancer construct for 15 min.
Wash the cancer construct three times with 1x PBS after fixing.
Treat the cancer construct with 500 μL of 0.1% Triton X-100 at room temperature for 5 min.
Wash the cancer construct three times with 1x PBS to remove Triton X-100.
Treat the cancer construct with 500 μL of 2% BSA using a pipette at room temperature for 1 h.
Cover the chip with paraffin film during the BSA treatment.
Wash the chip three times with 1x PBS after blocking.
Prepare isotype control antibodies in 1x PBS at the desired working concentration.
Dilute primary antibodies in 1x PBS to each desired working concentration.
Aspirate all 1x PBS from the chip using a pipette.
Treat the chip with 200 μL of primary antibody solution at 4 °C overnight.
Cover the chips with paraffin film to prevent evaporation.
Aspirate the primary antibody solution.
Wash the chip three times with 1x PBS.
Dilute secondary antibodies in 1x PBS at a ratio of 1:200.
Dilute DAPI in 1x PBS at a ratio of 1:1000.
Aspirate all 1x PBS from the chip using a pipette.
Treat the chip with 200 μL secondary antibody-DAPI solution at 4 °C for 3 h.
Cover the chip with paraffin film to prevent evaporation and wrap it with aluminum foil to prevent photobleaching.
Aspirate the secondary antibody-DAPI solution.
Wash the chip three times with 1x PBS.
Transfer the cancer construct to a confocal dish by gently gripping with forceps.
Visualize labeled cells using a confocal microscope.
Adjust the wavelength of the confocal microscope based on the type of fluorescent markers used.
Observe DAPI-stained nuclei first for better cell position detection.
Set excitation/emission wavelengths as 358/461 nm (DAPI, Blue), 494/517 nm (Green), and 590/617 nm (Red).
Use magnifications of 4x, 10x, and 20x for imaging.
Run an image processing program to count live and dead cells.
Open the fluorescent image files in the program.
Convert images to 16-bit grayscale by clicking Image | Type | 16-bit Grayscale.
Adjust threshold settings to make cell color black using Image | Adjust | Threshold.
Cut merged cells apart precisely with Process | Binary | Watershed.
Count the number of cells by selecting Analyze Particles three times under Analyze.
Calculate and present data as mean ± standard error.
